The reviewed 250F technical overview identifies the straight-six car, four-speed manual gearbox, clutch pedal and period cockpit controls; the AC package's four forward gears agree.

claims.basis: The reviewed 250F technical overview identifies the straight-six car, four-speed manual gearbox, clutch pedal and period cockpit controls; the AC package's four forward gears agree.

The technical overview and cockpit/control description identify a four-speed gearbox. The period cockpit description identifies a driver-operated small gear lever; this is the manual H-pattern control arrangement. The source explicitly identifies a clutch pedal; an H-pattern manual car needs it to launch from rest. Manual blip is modeled as a downshift action. Automatic blip is modeled as a downshift action. Throttle lift is modeled for upshift technique. No downshift cut action is documented. The inspected 250F cockpit images show a large continuous wooden round rim. The wheel has no readout; gauges are mounted separately. No wheel-mounted shift lights are visible. The photographed rim is closed and continuous. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/gearbox_type, /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
